headline: Tarique Rahman vows to keep anti-fascist alliance united during dinner meeting
summary: The BNP Chairman pledged to maintain unity among the 41 political parties that joined the anti-autocracy movement, emphasizing that people's interests come first.
details: Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman hosted a courtesy meeting and dinner for leaders of 41 allied political parties at the State Guest House Jamuna on Monday.

Tarique Rahman pledged to maintain unity among the parties that joined the anti-fascist movement, stating that his government would prioritize the interests of the people over political considerations.
Acknowledging the frustrations of alliance leaders, he expressed regret for any shortcomings and urged partners to remain patient as the government works to meet public expectations.
He clarified that while there may be different views on implementing the 31-point reform agenda, there is no misunderstanding or division among the allies, as they share a common goal.
Tarique noted that the government inherited a battered economy and damaged institutions, but has already begun implementing key commitments, such as waiving agricultural loans up to Tk 10,000.
He also mentioned the launch of Farmers’ Card and Family Card programs, alongside reforms in health, education, and expatriate welfare.

Tarique criticized a 'covert force' that is now claiming credit for the anti-autocracy movement despite being absent during the struggle, stating they only revealed themselves after the fall of the regime on August 5.
The event was attended by leaders of 41 parties, including Ganatantra Mancha, the 12-Party Alliance, Jatiyatabadi Samomona Jote, and others.

headline_marked: Airport arrest: [[Youth on 3-day remand]] for extremist links
headline: Airport arrest: Youth on 3-day remand for extremist links
summary: Md. Mamun Hossain was detained at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport while attempting to travel to Qatar on a worker visa.
details: A Dhaka court has granted a three-day remand for Md. Mamun Hossain, 26, who was arrested at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on suspicion of involvement with extremist organizations.
Mamun was detained by the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) from the airport's immigration detention room based on intelligence reports.
The state prosecutor alleged that Mamun has a history of extremist activities both domestically and internationally, including previous anti-terrorism cases in Bangladesh.
According to the prosecution, Mamun traveled to France via Portugal in 2020 and was deported back to Bangladesh for involvement in extremist activities that same year.
He is also allegedly linked to members of 'Fatah Combat,' a group arrested in the area of Jatrabari, Dhaka, which operated extremist activities under the guise of martial arts.
During the hearing, Mamun claimed he was innocent and was simply traveling to Qatar on a worker visa, asserting that he was on bail for previous cases and had no travel restrictions.
Mamun further alleged that in 2019, he was detained and forcibly interrogated by police after being stopped at the airport, claiming he was held incommunicado for 20 days.
The court rejected his bail plea and granted the remand to allow police to analyze his seized mobile phones and digital devices to identify associates and funding sources.
caption:
Detained while flying to Qatar, a youth with alleged extremist links is now on a 3-day police remand.

A Dhaka court has granted a three-day remand for Md. Mamun Hossain, 26, who was arrested at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on suspicion of involvement with extremist organizations.

Mamun was detained by the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) from the airport's immigration detention room based on intelligence reports.

The state prosecutor alleged that Mamun has a history of extremist activities both domestically and internationally, including previous anti-terrorism cases in Bangladesh.

According to the prosecution, Mamun traveled to France via Portugal in 2020 and was deported back to Bangladesh for involvement in extremist activities that same year.

He is also allegedly linked to members of 'Fatah Combat,' a group arrested in the area of Jatrabari, Dhaka, which operated extremist activities under the guise of martial arts.

During the hearing, Mamun claimed he was innocent and was simply traveling to Qatar on a worker visa, asserting that he was on bail for previous cases and had no travel restrictions.

Mamun further alleged that in 2019, he was detained and forcibly interrogated by police after being stopped at the airport, claiming he was held incommunicado for 20 days.

The court rejected his bail plea and granted the remand to allow police to analyze his seized mobile phones and digital devices to identify associates and funding sources.
